_: Main story beats (see docs/STORY.md and scripts/story.gd). %hero %pet %town %partner are filled in. A beat fires once; 'after' names a beat that must have fired first.

penguins.title: Chapter 1 — The Day the Star Crystal Came Down
penguins.summary: Something fell in your field and asked for help. The sky went red. Two brave penguins touched it.

lines.text: %town. Cobbles, a fountain that works on Tuesdays, a bell tower with no bell in it, and penguins at the edge of everything: on the walls, in the doorways, one asleep on the fountain. The island's old families. Nobody minds.
Everyone looks up when you pass, and then very carefully looks somewhere else. A town that has been waiting for something to happen for a long time, and isn't sure it wants it to.

effects.hint: Talk to everyone once. Maple sells seeds; Gideon fixes tools; the penguins keep to themselves, mostly.

lines.text: The sky over the east meadow goes a dark, dark red. Lightning, with no thunder after it. Then a howl: not a wolf. Lower, and sadder, and somehow angrier for being sad.
Oh no. They've come for the power. I hoped we'd have longer.

Listen, farmer. I ran from an army. The Grumps. They belong to the Dark Crystal, and he has felt me land. I've put a bubble over this farm; nothing of his can cross the fence after dark. But the meadow is outside the bubble, and so is the town.
Wooden sword, warm heart, east gate. And farmer: they weren't always Grumps. I'd rather show you than tell you.

effects.hint: The howling is in the east meadow. The farm is safe after dark; nothing else is.

lines.text: Where the Big Grump fell, the grass is green in a circle. In the middle of the circle: a collar. Leather, chewed, a brass tag worn smooth. BISCUIT. ...No. Not %pet. The tag is old.
The Dark Crystal doesn't make Grumps. He takes something that loved and squeezes until only the wanting is left. That was somebody's dog.

Long ago the star crystals learned that everyone needs love and happiness, and we made worlds where everyone had everything they needed. One of us decided power mattered more. He began to control the others. That's the army. That's him.

They can be turned back. Not beaten down: turned back. There's a magic for it, the Meow Pow Wow, and I only carry the first spark of it. The ones who truly know it are the cats of Cat-topia, and I hear them purring in the crystal meadow past the big one. We go there next.
The town doesn't know any of this. They think the meadow has wolves.
choice: Tell the town what the Grumps are.
Keep it quiet. They've got enough to worry about.

0.text: Brave. They'll look at every stray dog differently now. That might be good. It might be very hard.

1.text: Kind. And lonely. You'll be carrying it, then. I'll carry it with you.

0.hint: The town knows what Grumps are now. Alder will want to talk.

1.hint: Only you and Maple know. The collar is in your pack.

quest: cattopia
Find the purring in the crystal meadow: Cat-topia's cave.

penguins.title: Chapter 2 — Cat-topia
penguins.summary: The voice in the crystal meadow. Catkins teaches the Meow Pow Wow. The cave shakes.

lines.text: The crystal meadow. Purple and green, and rings of light turning slowly over it like a planet's rings seen from underneath. Past the standing stones, a mountain with a mouth, and a fog coming out of it.
And purring. Definitely purring. A dark figure walks out of the fog, takes down its hood, and is a cat.
Welcome to Cat-topia, farmer, and to the brave two. We're happy you survived the army of the Grumps. Come inside; it's warm, and it's time to learn your powers.

effects.hint: Talk to Catkins at the cave mouth in the crystal meadow.

lines.text: Inside it's warm. Cat treats everywhere, scratching posts, a hundred cats, and some of them flying. Nobody mentions the flying.
My name is Catkins, leader of Cat-topia. The star crystals gave us our magic too, long ago. Sit. All of you sit; this is the sad part.
The Dark Crystal wants to take away all the love and happiness in the universe. He controls other star crystals, and anyone they touch. That's a Grump: not a monster. Somebody, squeezed.
The only hope is to use the secret power of the star crystals against him. The Meow Pow Wow. It melts a grumpy heart, and the Grump remembers love and happiness, and helps us.
Hands make a heart at your chest. Hold it. Rainbow hearts and cat paws will fly out of you. Try. ...Yes. YES. A-meow-zing.
Something warm goes out of your chest in colours you don't have names for. Across the cave a very old cat stops frowning for the first time in years.

quest: spark
Build the Crystal Resonator from the Plans board by your house. Feed it crystal shards and it wakes the second spark.
effects.toast: Meow Pow Wow learned: tap ♥ with Nova (or any partner once they know it).

lines.text: You dream you're standing on a floor that breathes. Far below, something enormous beats, slow, like a heart that's been asleep a long while. The mountain's heart. Catkins called it Prismatica.
A voice, not the Star Crystal's. Older. "They keep digging. Let them. Every floor down is a floor closer to me."
You wake with grit under your fingernails. %pet is sitting up, staring at the floorboards.

effects.hint: The mine is the inside of the mountain. Something waits at the heart of it.

lines.text: There. The second spark. It's small, but it's yours, and it's the first one in a hundred years that wasn't mine.
Then the cave shakes. Crystals fall from the ceiling. Catkins meows loudly.
The Grumps have found our sacred island. They know we're the only ones with the magic to stop them. RUN. The catship is this way.
A ship shaped like an enormous cat, ears and all. Everyone aboard. The Grump ships are on its tail before it clears the meadow.
Don't worry. We have prepared for this. We have a very powerful secret weapon. Prepare the catapults, kitties.

The cats load the catapults with LITTER BOXES. Big Jim, if he's with you, says a word you don't repeat. The stink hits the Grump ships; they can't see; they crash, one after another, into the dark wastes past the meadow.

A-meow-zing! We've bought some time. Their Commander is down there in the Wastes. He was a person once. When you're ready, farmer: the Wastes gate opens for someone who can hold a sword like they mean it.

quest: wastes_gate
The Wastes gate opens when your sword arm is ready (Combat 3).
effects.toast: Litter Box: throw it; every Grump nearby stops to hold its nose.
effects.hint: Litter boxes stun Grumps. Catkins sells more at the cave mouth.

lines.text: The smoke clears. On the grey ground, where the Commander stood: a brass locket on a snapped chain. Inside, two boys on a dock, one holding a fish too big for him.
You know that dock. It's the lake. The smaller boy has Finn's ears.
...Oh. He went to the river cities, didn't he. Everyone who goes there comes back changed. The Dark Crystal has a man there in a grey suit. I've felt him. I don't know his name.
The locket is warm. It hums very faintly, like it's trying to remember a tune.
choice: Keep it. It's humming; that means something.

0.text: Yes. Whatever it costs him to hear it, he should hear it from someone who was there.

1.text: It's crystal-touched. It will know its own kind when it meets it. Don't lose it.

0.hint: Take the locket to Finn in town.

1.hint: The locket hums louder near crystals.

quest: sky_stair
Climb the great tree in the forest: the way up Mount Prismatica starts above the clouds.

lines.text: You hold out the locket. Finn doesn't take it. He looks at it the way you'd look at a wave that's going to hit you anyway.
Tomas. That's... that's the pike. He never caught anything bigger. Told everyone he did. Where did you—
No. Don't. I know where. I knew when he stopped writing. ...He ran, you said? Then he's still out there. Then he can still come home.
He'd have liked you. He liked anybody who'd walk into a field and swing at what was howling. Keep swinging, %hero. For both of us, yeah?
He takes the locket then, and turns toward the water so you won't see his face. You give him the water.

effects.hint: Finn knows. He says he'll row you across when the time comes.

penguins.title: Chapter 3 — Mount Prismatica
penguins.summary: Big Jim's campfire. The crystal babies. Coldy and the sacred key. A knight above the clouds.

lines.text: The mountain. Catkins said it: Prismatica. So tall the top is in space, and no ship can fly it; the magic won't allow it. It has to be climbed on foot.
The light on the rock changes as you watch: pink, then purple, then orange, then green. It gets colder every ten steps. The penguins don't mind. Anyone else does.

effects.hint: Climb. The pass is blocked by something small and loud.

lines.text: That night, something follows you up from the valley. Bushes. Footsteps. The penguins press close together. Out of the shadows jumps a large figure.
It's just me. It's Big Jim. I couldn't let you do this alone. I brought camp gear.

Marshmallows. Shooting stars. An aurora the colour of the inside of a crystal, and Big Jim in a heavy winter coat, saying the next days will be the hardest: mysteries to solve, and things in the hills that don't want you to pass.
Also I'm not carrying the litter boxes. I want that said now.

effects.hint: Big Jim camps with you from here on. The babies hold the pass.

lines.text: Round the corner: a baby girl, two feet tall, covered in crystals, angry, silent. Then she stamps. STAMP. STAMP. STAMP. And chants, deafeningly: BEE BOP BOO BABY. BEE BOP BOO BABY.
By Jove. That baby looks like she's made of crystals.
From every cave on every side: stamp, stamp, stamp. Hundreds of them pour out and block the path, and the leader GROWS, to five feet, and the circle closes. There's no room to run.
First guardians of the mountain, I'd say. How do we get past them?
The leader holds up her hand. Silence. She steps forward and asks, very seriously: "Bee bop boo baby?"
The penguins look at each other for a long while, and then chirp at her. She looks delighted.
Oh. Oh, I see. They've been cursed by the Dark Crystal: all they can say is that. You can understand them because of the magic. And you're going to lift it. The Meow Pow Wow.

effects.toast: Don't just fight them: tap ♥ (Meow Pow Wow) when they're low.
effects.hint: The babies are cursed, not evil. Turn them back with the Meow Pow Wow (tap the ♥ button).

lines.text: The spell can be seen from space. The crystals of the mountain make it brighter. A flash of white, and when the colours settle, the baby leader steps forward with a smile.
You saved us babies! ...What bring you to Mountain?
The penguins chirp for some time. She nods.
Yes. I understand. You come to improve Meow Pow Wow so you get big, strong, and save universe. We babies know you are good. We allow you to pass.
But I must come with you. I hold the sacred key to the heart of Mount Prismatica. And...

0.text: (whispering) There are secret spies of the Dark Crystal in these hills. Finargles. Very sneaky. You may need help.

1.text: Coldy. C-O-L-D-I-E. That is my real name. ...There are spies in these hills. Finargles. Very sneaky. We go quiet.

effects.hint: Coldy joined (the sacred key is a keepsake from the babies). Up: the great tree, then above the clouds.

lines.text: Above the clouds it is very quiet, and the islands float like they've forgotten what holding on is for. It's dark up here even at noon; the stars are out.
We are surrounded. The finargles are here.
The shadows between the islands have grown thicker. Something black and fuzzy, the size of a large pumpkin, with two eyes and no mouth, watches you from each one.
On the far island, a figure in blue-white armour, perfectly still. Frost on its shoulders with the same pattern as the frost on your gate the morning the penguins came.
That's a penguin, farmer. Or was. Older than the brave two put together. The Dark Crystal doesn't only make Grumps; sometimes he makes guards.

effects.hint: Finargles: purple eye-light dazes you. The Crystal Knight on the far island; Nova would know him.

lines.text: ...Grandfather Auk. He went to find the crystal before I hatched. They said the mountain took him.
The mountain didn't. It was this. I can feel him in there, under the glass. The Meow Pow Wow reaches bigger things every time I use it. I don't know if it reaches that big.
The Knight turns its head. Slowly. Toward Nova, not you.
choice: Let Nova try the Meow Pow Wow first.

0.text: Keep him off me for ten seconds. That's all. Ten.
She makes the heart at her chest, and the clouds go still to listen.

1.text: ...Right. Crack that armour open, then, and get him out of there.

0.hint: Tap ♥ near the Knight when he's below a third of his strength: Nova's Meow Pow Wow.

lines.text: In the glass, as it goes, a face. Old, tired, not unkind. It says one thing, so quietly the clouds nearly take it:
A man in a grey suit bargains with him. Under the river cities. He thinks he's winning.
A man, choosing it. That's worse, farmer. That's much worse.

quest: teleporter
The top of the mountain is in space. Power the moon teleporter with 3 Refined Crystals, then face the spire.
effects.hint: The moon station's teleporter needs 3 Refined Crystals. The resonator makes them.

lines.text: He heard me. At the end. I don't know if that's better. I think it's better.
When we go up there, to the heart: he'll be there. I don't know how I know. I know.
Among the shards, one that doesn't melt. Warm, heavy, and when you pick it up your sword hand stops aching.
If Nova is with you, she kneels by a line of small webbed footprints leading up into the cloud. 'He ran. He's still in there somewhere. I'll find him.'

effects.toast: Knight's Shard: your sword hits harder.

penguins.title: Chapter 4 — The Finargles and the Merkitties
penguins.summary: A crystal prison. A question in your head. The uphill stream, the waterfall, and the song that gives you a tail.

lines.text: You don't see it happen. A small black shape in a crack of shadow; purple light from two eyes; and you can't move a muscle. A flash. And you are somewhere else: a room of crystal, no door, and your friends beside you, blinking.
We are caught by very powerful finargles. Most finargles do not have those abilities until they are teenagers. At least ten thousand years old.
*Who are you, and why do you climb Mount Prismatica?*
They are telepathic. They talk in our minds. They have no mouths.
*The Dark Crystal has promised me I will be queen of this mountain once he has defeated the two too powerful penguins. He says he wants to make the universe a perfect paradise. Why do you fight him?*
choice: Tell her the truth: what he does to the ones he promises things to.
Tell her nothing. Look for a way out.

0.text: The penguins chirp for a long time. Silence. Then: *The Dark Crystal said you would lie to me about him. I will not be deceived.* ...But the voice is slower than it was, and it doesn't come back for a while.

1.text: *Very soon the Dark Crystal will be told that I have you.* The voice goes. The room is very quiet.

lines.text: Floor. We drill. Meow Pow Wow at the floor; the mountain listens to it.

The spell goes down instead of out, and the crystal under you goes soft, and then it isn't there. You fall into fast dark water that carries you UP, through the mountain, for what feels like hours, everyone holding hands. Big Jim: "I see a light!" And then you are in open air, and falling, down a waterfall, into a jungle, into a pool, into black.

effects.hint: You washed out at the lake. Someone pulled you from the water.

lines.text: You wake on the shore with the sun going down, and no idea how you got out of the water. A blue-green glow comes toward you through it: a cat with a tail, wearing a glowing necklace.
Oh good. You've all woken. We found you after the waterfall; you were in a bad way. We've been hiding you. The finargles have been through here looking for you, so we've made you invisible to them.

More glows in the water. Mercats. One of them: "Mer, the finargles have told the Dark Crystal. The Grumps are coming to the mountain, and the whole surface is swarming with spies looking for our new friends."
Then we share our merkitty magic, and take them through the under-mountain ocean tunnels to the very top. Everyone into the pool.
I don't know about that. What do these muscly catfish want to do to us?

Everyone into the pool. The merkitties swim a circle around you, singing, and their necklaces glow, and all at once you have a tail. Mer: "You can become a mermaid now, any time you enter water." Big Jim screams. He screams for some time. Everyone wears earplugs until he stops.

effects.toast: The merkitties' gift: you grow a tail in any water. Swim anywhere.
effects.hint: You can swim and dive anywhere now. The way to the top is the mountain pad now.

lines.text: It remembers where it goes. So do I. I wasn't sure I would.
Before we go: the bell. Alder's been asking. A town that rings its bell is a town that's awake, and the Dark Crystal has never once beaten a town that was awake.
Not an order. A hope. Go home first, farmer. Sleep. Say goodbye to the field like you'll see it again, because you will.

effects.hint: The bell needs a gold clapper (Alder). When you're ready: the moon (mountain pad), then touch the crystal spire.

lines.text: The bell rings. Twenty-one years of rust come off it in one note, and the note goes out over the fields and the lake and the mine and comes back smaller and nicer.
My father pulled this rope. Everyone's in the plaza. Everyone. I didn't tell them to come.
You didn't have to. That's what a bell is for.

effects.hint: The bell rang, and the whole town came to the plaza. (If the fight on the moon is still ahead, they will remember it there.)

lines.text: Morning. Frost on the gate again, though it isn't the season for it. %partner is waiting there, and so, a little apart, is whoever else still counts you a friend.
So. The top of the mountain. In space. I always said I'd go somewhere nobody had been. I meant the next valley over.
The pad on the mountain goes to the moon: that IS the top, farmer; the mountain reaches that far. The crystal spire, right there on the moon. That's where he is. That's where he's always been.
%pet barks once, at nothing, the way dogs do when they've decided.

effects.hint: Mountain pad → moon → the crystal spire (just north of the teleporter).

penguins.title: Chapter 5 — The Heart of Mount Prismatica
penguins.summary: The spire is the Dark Crystal. The finargle queen stands with him. Whatever you kept, and whoever you kept, comes with you.

lines.text: The spire isn't a spire. It's a crystal the size of a church, grown out of the top of the mountain where it pierces the sky, and it is dark the way a closed eye is dark.
Sister. You brought a FARMER. And the two little birds.
I brought friends. You remember those. You had some.
I remember being left. I remember every kind thing, and how little it weighed when it mattered. Power weighs. The man in the grey suit knows it. The queen of this mountain knows it. So will you.

*I told you he would come,* says a voice in your head, and a black fuzzy shape the size of a pumpkin rises beside the dark, crowned in purple light. Fennimore. The ground shivers. Shapes pull themselves out of the dark like they've been waiting for their cue.
*...You said he squeezes the ones he promises things to.* The purple light around Fennimore flickers. *I have been promised things.*
She's listening, farmer. Turn her back, don't break her. She'll remember.

effects.toast: Fennimore hesitates: she can be turned back with the Meow Pow Wow.

lines.text: From very far away, carried on nothing at all: a bell. One note, twenty-one years of rust, and then voices under it. The whole town, in the plaza, saying your name.
...What is that. What IS that.
That's weight. The kind you forgot.

effects.toast: The Dark Crystal's shell cracks: it's half as strong.

lines.text: On the ridge, blue-white and transparent, a penguin the size of a door. He doesn't fight. He stands between the shards and Nova, and the shards won't go near him.
Grandfather.

effects.toast: Grandfather Auk holds the shards off.

lines.text: And beside the crystal, in the dark, someone you know. They don't look at you. You did that, a long time ago now, at a gate.
You see? Everyone you leave comes to me. Everyone.

effects.toast: A bitter companion stands with the Dark Crystal.

lines.text: It stops. Not dead; stopped, the way a held breath is stopped. In the cracks, something flickers that isn't dark.
Pieces are missing from it. Clean breaks, like someone has been chipping splinters off and carrying them away, down toward the city.
Now. While it's quiet. Farmer: the Meow Pow Wow. The real one, the one Catkins meant. Hands at your chest. It's been in you since the cave.

choice: Make the heart. Turn him back.
Break the dark. Let it end.

0.text: You put your hands at your chest, and you think about the collar, and the locket, and the bell, and the gate, and the babies stamping, and Big Jim screaming about tails, and rainbow hearts and cat paws come out of you so bright they can see them from the island.
The dark goes grey. The grey goes glass. The glass goes bright, bright, BRIGHT — and there are two crystals on the top of the mountain, and they are both crying, if crystals can.
...Sister. I'm so tired.
I know. Come home. There's a field.
*...Oh,* says a small voice in your head, and the purple light around Fennimore goes out, and she is just a fuzzy black thing the size of a pumpkin, blinking, with no mouth to say sorry.

1.text: You let the light go the other way. The dark comes apart the way ice goes on a pond in spring: all at once, and then quietly, for a long time.
...That was my brother. He isn't, right now. But he was, and maybe one day he will be again.
The Grumps will stop. The man in the grey suit won't. But that's a different story, and someone else's.

effects.hint: Go home. Sleep. See what the morning says.

lines.text: Morning. The field. The Star Crystal is in the middle of it, half-buried, like it's been planted. She has.
I asked him where he wanted to be. He said: somewhere things grow. I said I knew a place.
He wouldn't come home. He's gone somewhere far off to think about what he did. So I planted something anyway, where he used to stand, so that something would grow there.
At the gate, a dog. Old, grey at the muzzle, a brass tag worn smooth. It looks at the house like it's been away a long time and isn't sure of its welcome. %pet runs to it. That settles that.

On the fence, two penguins, brother and sister, watching the sun come up over the island the way they must have watched the crystal come down. One of them chirps. You're fairly sure it means: what's next?
There's always another chapter. But not today. Today there's turnips.

effects.toast: Thank you for playing. The farm goes on.

gangsters.title: Chapter 1 — Lie Low
gangsters.summary: A deed with the wrong name. A letter. Somebody already knows.

lines.text: %town. The kind of place where nobody asks your name because they've already decided what it is.
A store, a smith, a clinic, a town hall with a bell tower and no bell. A woman on the bench by the gate who watches the road the way you watch it. Sal.

effects.hint: Sal on the bench by the south gate has been places. Maple sells seeds and asks no questions.

lines.text: The President's man stumbles off between the rocks and is gone, leaving his coat behind. In it, a photograph of your old front door, and a phone with one number in it.
You don't call it. You think about it for a long time, and then you don't.
Written on the back of the photograph, in a hand with hard loops on the W and a hard press on the K: "WE KNOW ABOUT THE FARM. NICE TOUCH."
choice: Hold it up to what you remember of the first note.

0.text: Ash in the meadow grass. It's getting to be a habit.

1.text: Two pieces of paper now. A case, almost.

2.text: Same W. Same K. You'd bet the farm on it, and you've only got the one.

quest: hideout
Get through the gate to Hideout town and find a place to work from.
effects.hint: Sal says the hideout gate is past the meadow outskirts. Talk to her first.

lines.text: Hideout town. Past the outskirts, through a gate that doesn't look like a gate. Deuce deals cards there, Mama Rosa feeds whoever's left, nobody runs the street. That's the opening.
You'll want people. Not thugs; those are a crystal a dozen. People. Ones who want something you can give them.
And boss? The President doesn't send one man. He sends one man, and then he sends the weather.

effects.hint: Hideout town: Deuce (card table), Mama Rosa (kitchen door). Recruit people, not thugs.

gangsters.title: Chapter 2 — The Hideout
gangsters.summary: A town that isn't on maps. Two recruits. A shop, if you want one, and what it costs.

lines.text: Up close: the motel's half-lit sign, the diner's burnt coffee smell, the drive-in screen with a crown painted on it. Everybody here came from somewhere they can't go back to, which makes you a local.
A man at a folding table dealing cards to nobody. A woman in a doorway with a rolling pin and an expression. Two people who want something.

effects.hint: Deuce at the card table; Mama Rosa at the kitchen door. Each wants something before they'll join.

lines.text: Sit. No? Then stand, it's your knees. I'm Deuce. I deal, I don't cheat, which is why I'm here and not uptown.

You're building something. I can tell; you've got the look of a man counting. I'm in, for a fee. A hundred and fifty, or beat me at one friendly hand of cards, nothing on the table, and I'll call it paid.

0.text: Cash. Boring. Effective. Welcome to the crew, boss; I'll keep the books.

1.text: He deals. You lose. He deals again, slower, and you watch his left thumb, and you win.
...You watched the thumb. Nobody watches the thumb. Fine. FINE. I'm in, and I'm never playing you again.

lines.text: You're thin. Everyone who comes through that gate is thin. I had a kitchen in the river cities that fed forty men a night and none of them ever said thank you, and then it burned.
Bring me ten of anything you grew with your own hands. Ten. Then we'll talk about whose crew I'm cooking for.

0.text: She weighs each one in her hand like it might be lying.
...Dirt under the nails. All right, farmer. I'm in. Somebody in this crew is going to eat properly.

1.text: The door's open. It's always open. That's the problem with it.

lines.text: Boss. The bakery in %town. Woman who runs it is sweet, and the lease is a joke, and the back room has a door onto the alley.
An arcade there pays the crew for a season. She'd have to go, of course. Somewhere nice. We'd make sure.
choice: No. Not her shop. Not anyone's.

0.text: That's the counting look. I like the counting look. I'll send the boys with a polite letter.
Three days later, the bakery is boarded, and there's a man in a good coat on the avenue at night who nods when you pass.

1.text: ...Huh. All right. I've worked for worse reasons. We'll make money the slow way; I hear it keeps.

0.hint: Posy's bakery is an arcade now. A thug walks the avenue at night.

quest: docks
The docks move everything. Take them from the dock boss.

gangsters.title: Chapter 3 — The Docks
gangsters.summary: Crates with purple crystals in them. Three recruits. A fence with an offer.

lines.text: The manifest. Every crate marked with a small purple crystal, and every destination the same: UPTOWN, TOWER, SUB-BASEMENT 3.
He isn't moving money. He's moving something that eats money, and luck, and whole towns. You've seen the colour before. In the meadow, in the thing that was his man.
Someone who can read a manifest like a map would be worth a lot right now. The girl with the laptop in the warehouse doorway hasn't looked up once. She's looked up three times.

effects.hint: Specs (warehouse door) wants the manifest. Ladder is up the crane. Halo races on the dock road.

lines.text: Don't say anything. Give me the paper. ...Yes. YES. Sub-basement three. I knew it had a basement. Buildings like that always have a basement.
I'm Specs. I'm in. I was in before you got here; I just hadn't told you. Keep the paper, I've got it memorised. Don't lose the paper.
From up here you can see the whole dock, the whole road, and about a third of the tower. I've been counting trucks. Four hundred and twelve.
I don't fight. I see. You want someone who sees, I'm yours. You want someone who fights, ask the twins; they're always looking for a reason.

effects.hint: Ladder counts trucks. He'll warn you before a raid.

lines.text: Race you. Dock road, end to end, your legs against my car. I'll give you the first fifty yards because I'm a gentleman.
You don't win. Nobody wins against Halo. But you don't stop, either, and when she pulls up at the end you're still coming, and she watches you come.
Most people quit at the containers. I drive for people who don't quit at the containers. I'm in.

effects.hint: Halo can drive you between the gangster districts (talk to her at the hideout).

lines.text: You're the farmer with the paper. Don't look surprised; it's my business to know who has paper. I'm Marlene. I buy things people shouldn't have.
A letter, in a certain hand, with a certain W. There are people who'd pay to have it not exist. Two thousand. Tonight.
choice: Sell it. ◆2000 buys a lot of crew.

0.text: Sensible. Paper is only worth what someone fears it for. ...He'll know your face by the weekend, you understand. That's the price under the price.

1.text: Then it's worth more than two thousand, and you know it. Keep it dry. I'm in, by the way. I like a man who knows what he's holding.

0.hint: The President knows your face now.

quest: neon

A letter, in a certain hand, with a certain W. There are people who'd pay to have it not exist. Two thousand. Tonight.
choice: Sell it. ◆2000 buys a lot of crew.

0.text: Sensible. Paper is only worth what someone fears it for. ...He'll know your face by the weekend, you understand. That's the price under the price.

1.text: Then it's worth more than two thousand, and you know it. Keep it dry. I'm in, by the way. I like a man who knows what he's holding.

quest: neon
Put out Flame in the neon district.

lines.text: You're the farmer with the paper. Don't look surprised; it's my business to know who has paper. I'm Marlene. I buy things people shouldn't have.
There was a letter, in a certain hand, with a certain W. People would have paid to have it not exist. Then I hear you burned it on your first night.
So you're the only person in this city with nothing to sell me. I find that... restful. I'm in. Somebody should fence for you who isn't an idiot.

gangsters.title: Chapter 4 — Neon
gangsters.summary: A dragon sign, a pit under the street, and six more who might follow you.

lines.text: Neon. Rain that's pink on one side of the street and blue on the other. Under the dragon sign, a woman who sets things on fire for a living, and a crowd pretending not to watch her do it.
Down a stairwell with no sign: the sound of a crowd that isn't pretending anything.

effects.hint: Flame under the dragon sign. The pit is down the unmarked stairs.

lines.text: The flames go out. The crowd, very quietly, starts to clap. A pair of identical faces in red and blue stop clapping first and look at each other.
Pit's open.
We fight the winner.
We ARE the winner.
That's what I said.

quest: pit
Win the fight pit under the neon street.
effects.hint: The twins fight in the pit. Dice owes the pawnbroker for a busted scooter; the Kid lost his board; Doc wants herbs; Sasha is the ring's muscle.

lines.text: ...Okay.
Okay.
We're in. Both of us. You don't get one.
Nobody gets one.

effects.toast: Vic and Val joined the crew.

lines.text: I'm not— look, I run things. Messages. Small things. I borrowed the pawnbroker's scooter and I wrecked it. Three hundred to fix, and he's started saying my name in a voice.
Clear it and I'm yours. I'm fast and I'm scared and both of those are useful.
choice: Go have a word with the pawnbroker.

0.text: You— just like that? Boss. BOSS. Okay. Okay okay okay. I'm in.

1.text: The pawnbroker is a man at a counter under a bare bulb, winding and rewinding a watch he never sells. You don't say anything. You put your hand flat on the counter, and you leave it there, and after a while he nods.
What did you SAY to him? He gave me my dice back. He never gives anything back.

lines.text: No. No, I know who you are, your face is on a— he's got your FACE, man. I run messages. I'm not running yours.
He's gone before you can answer. Marlene did say there was a price under the price.
The hood doesn't move. After a while a hand comes out of it and makes a shape: a board, wheels, gone.
Flame's guys took it. Under the dragon. It's got a sticker of a cat.
Under the dragon sign, in a pile of what used to be Flame's things: a board with a cat sticker. You bring it back. The hood nods once, which you're told later is a speech.
Sit. Let me see that arm. ...You hold a sword like a hoe. That's not an insult; hoes are honest.
I patched people for a man uptown, once. I stopped. Bring me five wild herbs from the forest and I'll patch for you instead, and I'll do it properly.

0.text: Good roots. Good. I'm in, boss. Try not to need me.

1.text: I'll be here. I'm always here.

lines.text: You beat the champion. The champion was soft. I'm the one who carries the champion out.
I don't join. I follow. Walk out of here and don't look back to see if I'm coming, and we'll both find out.
You walk out. You don't look back. At the top of the stairs, a shadow the size of a doorway falls over yours.
The arcade's doing great, boss. The painter's studio next door — Lumi? — has room for a second floor of games. She'd land on her feet. Painters do.

0.text: Lumi leaves on the morning bus with a canvas under each arm and doesn't look at the arcade. Two men in good coats on the avenue now.

1.text: You're a soft touch for a boss. I keep forgetting I like that.

lines.text: Last one. The clinic. I know. I KNOW. But we could run it, and the woman there — Juniper — she's been sending letters to the capital about us, boss. I read them.

0.text: Juniper doesn't leave quietly. She stands in the plaza and says what you are, to everyone, and then she goes. The bell tower stays empty. Nobody would pull the rope for you now.

1.text: ...Good. I was hoping you'd say that. Don't tell the boys.

gangsters.title: Chapter 5 — Uptown
gangsters.summary: The tower. The doors. The man with the stone in his chest.

lines.text: The doors are brass and twelve feet tall and have a slot in them like a mailbox. You know what goes in the slot. You've known since the rain.
The letter goes in. Somewhere inside, a mechanism that has been waiting for exactly this paper, this hand, this W, turns over once.
The doors open. Nobody fights you. That was the point of keeping it.

effects.hint: The doors are open. The lobby.

lines.text: Stand back. I used to clean these doors. The service lock still takes my old key.
A click, a sigh of brass, and the tower doors swing in without a sound.

effects.hint: The lobby is quiet. Nobody knows you're in.

lines.text: The doors are brass and twelve feet tall and have a slot in them like a mailbox. The letter has been folded into the deed since the rain.
It goes in. Somewhere inside, a mechanism turns over once, and the doors open. Nobody fights you.

effects.hint: The doors are open. The lobby.

lines.text: The doors are brass and twelve feet tall and have a slot in them like a mailbox. The letter is still in your coat, read so many times it's soft.
It goes in. Somewhere inside, a mechanism turns over once, and the doors open. Nobody fights you.

effects.hint: The doors are open. The lobby.

lines.text: Brass, twelve feet tall, a slot like a mailbox. Whatever was supposed to go in it, you don't have it any more.
Move.
Your crew put their shoulders to the brass together, and the mechanism inside gives with a sound like a bell that's been dropped.
Every light in the tower comes on at once. So much for quiet.

effects.hint: The lobby. They know you're coming.

lines.text: The lobby is marble and empty and very, very cold. At the far end, a man in a grey suit in a chair that is too big for him, and in his chest, where a pocket square should be, a purple stone the size of a fist, pulsing.
He turns the chair. You know the face. You've known it longer than you've known your own name: the man who got you out of the city with a coat over your head and a deed in your pocket.
Hello, kid. You read my letters. Burned, kept, memorised: I wrote every one of them so you'd do exactly what you did. M. was always me.
The note on the envelope, the hard loops on the W? My other hand. You only ever saw me write with the right. I made sure of that.
I put your hands on that deed. I sent the man with the photograph so you'd be angry enough to climb my stairs. And here you are. You always did come when I called.
Twenty-one years ago a star fell in your field. I took one piece and left the rest under the soil, waiting for someone it would trust. It trusts you. I made sure of that, too.
You met my young people on the way up. I gave each of them a splinter of this, one black stone pressed into a cold hand on a bad day. Every Gift in this city is the same stone, and the stone is mine.
It promised me nobody would ever leave me again. Everybody leaves, kid. So I stopped needing anyone to stay. Come and see what that buys.
I've got the patching up, boss. You've got him. Remember what I said.
He's on his knees on the marble. The stone in his chest is cracked and dark and it's whispering, and you realise you've been hearing it since the meadow.
Take it. The city. The chair. You've earned it; you counted every step. Put your hand on the stone and keep counting.

choice: Pull the stone out of him.
Put your hand on it. Take the city.

0.text: It comes loose with a sound like a cork. He gasps, once, and then he's just an old man in a bad suit on a cold floor, looking at his hands like they're new.
...I was going to come out to the farm. One spring. Help you plant, and tell you all of it. It said I didn't need to. It said you'd come to me.
You put the stone on the marble and you break it with your heel, and the whisper stops, and somewhere above the city a very old bell that was never going to ring again rings once anyway.
All over the city the splinters go quiet. A girl on the docks watches the flame in her palm gutter, and then, slowly, come back smaller, and steadier, and hers.
The Gifts stay. They are only what they always were underneath: ten young people who were told a stone made them worth something, finding out it was the other way round.

1.text: It's warm. That's the surprise. It's warm, and it's grateful, and it's got so many plans.
Later, in the chair, you write a letter to someone who's gone to ground on a farm. You tell them the farm is a nice touch. You notice, as you seal it, the hard loops on the W.
Across the city, ten splinters warm in ten pockets, and ten young people turn toward the tower without knowing why. They work for you now. They always did work for the stone.

effects.hint: Go home. Sleep. See who's in the plaza.

lines.text: Morning. Rain again, the collar kind. The deed on the table still has the wrong name on it, and you find you don't mind; names are things you can grow into.
At the gate, the crew. All of them, the ones who stayed, leaning on Halo's car like they've been there since before the sun. Sal at the front.
Boss. The town's in the plaza. Or what's left of it. They're not sure what you are. Neither am I.
Go find out. We'll mind the farm. Somebody's got to water the turnips.

effects.toast: Thank you for playing. The farm goes on.
